currentShow.title: Underwater Cats
currentShow.description: The work consists of cats hanging out on window sills from the notable Roblox game, Bloxburg. The area outside the windows consists of an actual aquarium, while inside the windows shows a rainy day. This work consists of lots of greenscreening as I layer the components of reality (with the cats, aquarium, and windows) with fantasy.

currentShow.title: Device and Method for Reducing Brain Valve Regurgitation
currentShow.description: This work originates from found medical imagery discovered in the Google Patents archive. I was drawn to these scans because they already felt like completed artworks: anonymous, clinical, accidental images hiding in the depths of technical infrastructure and search engines. Removed from their original function, they become uncanny visual objects suspended between diagnosis, abstraction, and machine-made composition. By reframing this image as video art, the work asks what can be considered an artwork in the era of post-internet circulation, cyborg aesthetics, and endless image extraction. If an image can be generated for purely technical or biomedical purposes yet still produce affect, fascination, and formal intensity, where does art begin and where does utility end? In this sense, "Device and Method for Reducing Brain Valve Regurgitation" is less an act of invention than of recognition. It treats the internet not only as an archive, but as a site where latent artworks already exist. The piece reflects on authorship, appropriation, and the strange beauty of images produced beyond artistic intention.

currentShow.title: Digital Anima(l)
currentShow.description: Digital Anima(l) is part of my ongoing exploration of technological and sacred: the possibility that something like soul, aura, or inner life can reappear through synthetic image-making. The work began with footage of a real running horse, which I processed through AI image generation using Stable Diffusion. Through this translation, the animal body was transformed into a luminous, unstable apparition, no longer fully biological, but not fully artificial either. In the context of the post-physical, this work imagines the animal as data-body, phantom, and digital soul. It asks whether technological mediation can produce new forms of presence rather than simply flattening the real. The horse appears here as both living source and synthetic afterimage.

currentShow.title: Arts and Leisure (Crying)
currentShow.description: Arts and Leisure (Crying) examines the tension between authenticity and performance. Crying is presented as both intimate and mediated, inviting uncertainty around sincerity. Through repetition, the work highlights the act of looking, suggesting how vulnerability becomes aestheticized and consumed, where genuine emotion and performance collapse into one another.

currentShow.title: Untitled (0x0000001A)
currentShow.description: Untitled (0x0000001A) was born from revisiting documentation I shot in 2024. This video is a selected portion of a longer video which I manipulated into what you see now. The process was incredibly intuitive after spending months researching-watching films and reading books. Asking myself how I could bring absurdity into my work. I knew it was time to sort out my thoughts and bring them into fruition. I was itching for it. The entire video is going through this process of deterioration with this blue colored effect, #0000FF to be exact. That hex code belongs to the infamous "Blue Screen of Death", or bsod for short, which happens to Windows computers when something goes wrong-very wrong. In this case, I refer to an error code pop-up meaning the PC has insufficient RAM. Think of RAM as part of the computer's brain, where its memories are stored. When there isn't enough storage, things aren't saved and memories become false. The bsod isn't something you want to see.

currentShow.title: Survey
currentShow.medium: Generative mixed media digital installation; artist-built control pedestal and mounted screen displaying the real-time output of a graphics shader. Real-time variable length, resolution, and aspect ratio.
currentShow.description: In this interactive viewer-curated installation, participants are invited to navigate and document an endless generative landscape as it warps below. Using the artist-built custom control panel, they can adjust their speed and heading as well as take snapshots with the central button (which are then automatically uploaded to a publicly available web viewer). The landscape actively resists capture; structures begin to twist and change beneath a stationary lens and attempts to return to previously seen terrain are met with the dissolution of the familiar. This piece explores themes of fomo, shared experience, and the beauty of geology through the lens of physically interactive shader art. please consider viewing the collection of viewer-captured images at: https://surveysorties.com/

currentShow.title: One Last Shot
currentShow.description: "One Last Shot" is part of a series of video collages in which the viewer is bombarded with sound and image scraped from the internet, samples recontextualized and distorted, a dysphoric scream of anguish, but also a celebration of the absurd, and the bizarre, disgusting world of the computer, the human body, and self destruction.
